title: Ingress Policy Compiler — slate
summary: Personal sketch for a small compiler that converts high-level ingress/routing policy DSL into per-cluster route configs + cost-aware fallbacks. Focus: compact DSL, predictable semantics, ability to target model variants, and produce explainable rollout plans.
content:
Purpose / motivation:

Small personal draft for an "ingress policy compiler" that sits between the API surface (per-tenant route rules in YAML/JSON) and the runtime route tables used by the serving mesh. Goal: let product/platform folks express intent at a human scale (SLA, cost tier, latency priority, fallback strategy) and compile that to concrete runtime artifacts (route priorities, model variant pins, region hints, throttles, canary weights).

Why this? We keep adding ad-hoc routing flags across codepaths. Need a single source-of-truth language that is:
- readable by SREs and SEs
- small enough to be reviewed in PRs
- expressive enough to capture cost/latency tradeoffs and fallbacks
- deterministic to allow rollbacks and diffs

Non-goals (for now):
- full policy engine for auth/ABAC
- multi-tenant isolation beyond standard tenant-id scoping
- replacing existing SLA dashboards

High-level semantics (brain dump):
- Top-level object: policy-set for a tenant or product route.
- Policies are ordered: earlier policies are higher priority unless explicit match weight specified.
- Match clauses: route path, model family regex, hint tags (e.g., vpc-only, dedicated), client attributes (tier, quota-state).
- Actions: route to model variant, rewrite prompt, attach a pre-warm hint, set batching profile, set cost-target (hard or soft), set fallback chain.
- Compiler emits: runtime-route (JSON), rollout-plan (canary weights + duration), telemetry-bindings (span tags), cost-estimate (tokens/sec * cost model).

DSL sketch (informal pseudo-YAML):

policy_set: "search-api-ingress-v1"
owner: "product-search"
policies:
  - id: "low-latency-path"
    match:
      path_prefix: "/v1/search"
      client_tier: premium
      latency_slo_ms: 200
    action:
      model: "rw-llama-13b-low-latency"
      batching_profile: "tiny"
      cost_target: "soft:0.8"   # prefer cheaper variants when load high
      on_failure: "fallback:rw-llama-13b-quantized,route:rw-llama-7b"
      telemetry_labels: ["slo:low-latency","route:fast"]

  - id: "cost-led-path"
    match:
      path_prefix: "/v1/search"
      client_tier: standard
    action:
      model: "rw-llama-13b-quantized"
      batching_profile: "balanced"
      cost_target: "hard:0.5"   # maximum expected cost multiplier
      fallback_chain: ["rw-llama-7b","rw-llama-3b"]

Notes on the above:
- cost_target semantics: soft means compiler can pick a cheaper variant or enable stronger batching; hard means compile-time validation fails if estimated cost exceeds target.
- on_failure vs fallback_chain: on_failure is runtime detected (OOM, node-crash) fallback; fallback_chain is precomputed route order for load-shedding.

Compiler outputs (examples):
1) runtime-route JSON (flattened for the serving runtime)
{
  "route_id":"search-api-ingress-v1:low-latency",
  "match": {"path_prefix":"/v1/search", "client_tier":"premium"},
  "backend_chain": [
    {"model":"rw-llama-13b-low-latency","weight":100},
    {"model":"rw-llama-13b-quantized","weight":0, "conditions":["cost>0.9"]}
  ],
  "batching_profile":"tiny",
  "telemetry_tags":["slo:low-latency","route:fast"]
}

2) rollout-plan artifact (human-friendly):
- step 1: seed 5% traffic to rw-llama-13b-low-latency in region us-west2 for 6h, monitor p99 latency and error-rate
- step 2: increase to 25% if error < 0.5% and p99 < 220ms for 30m
- step 3: full roll once no regressions for 24h

Compiler responsibilities checklist (what it must do):
- Validate policy semantics (no circular fallbacks, missing model variants).
- Expand shorthand (e.g., "cost-led" -> specific batching+tuning profiles).
- Run a local cost prediction model to annotate estimated per-1000-token cost for each route; fail early on hard limits.
- Emit deterministic hashes for artifact ids to allow diff/rollback.
- Attach explainability notes: which rule produced which routing table entry.

API shapes (sketch of the REST endpoint users will call):
POST /v1/ingress-policies/apply
Body: { policy_set: string, spec: string (YAML), dry_run: bool }
Response: { status: string, artifacts: [string (artifact ids)], diagnostics: [string], cost_estimate: string }

Implementation notes / rough plan:
- start with a thin Go binary that parses YAML -> internal AST -> validator -> emitter. Keep runtime library minimal.
- store artifacts in GCS + a small metadata table (Datastore/PG) containing compiled sha, owner, created_at.
- CI: policy PRs run a compile-and-dry-run job that posts diagnostics to PR.
- runtime integration: serving mesh consumes artifact via a simple GET /deployments/:artifactID and validates the signature.

Open design questions (personal TODOs):
- Where to put the cost model? Inline in compiler or remote service? Prefer small client embedded model to get fast feedback, remote call for production re-eval.
- How much of rollout orchestration does the compiler produce vs. the deployment system? produce only weights + timers or full automation?
- Prefer explicit weights (0-100) vs fuzzy (canary_percentage: 5). How to express ramping curves?
- How to version policies in a tenant-aware way so we can roll back to a previous compiled artifact across Dedicated clusters?

Safety & reliability notes:
- Compiler should refuse to emit artifacts that contain fallbacks to opt-in experimental models unless tenant has flag.
- Must annotate telemetry bindings so SLO dashboards can auto-wire new routes.

Edge-case fiddly bits:
- model alias resolution: policy references can be names (rw-llama-13b) that map to multiple compatible binary variants; compiler should prefer the stable variant unless cost_target suggests a quantized one.
- prewarm hints: action can ask runtime to pre-warm KV caches for a model id; compiler can add a prewarm TTL and priority to the artifact.
- if a policy has both hard cost_target and latency_slo, need a tie-break priority (default: latency > cost for "premium" clients).

Work items / next steps (short):
- prototype parser and AST for the DSL (week 1)
- implement validator rules and simple emitter that outputs runtime-route JSON (week 2)
- wire up a PR check to run compiler dry-run (week 3)
- demo with Search team: two routes, show cost vs latency tradeoff (week 4)

Personal notes to self / to discuss with Marisol:
- show tradeoff table: latency-cost for rw-llama-13b variants (use offline perf numbers).
- confirm naming convention for artifact ids with Riley (we need stable, short ids).
- think about how rules interact with tenant quotas (if quota exhausted, route should downgrade to cheaper model).

Rough TODO list (simple):
- [ ] finalize DSL minimal grammar
- [ ] AST unit tests for circular fallback detection
- [ ] emitter deterministic-hash test
- [ ] add cost-model stub and fixture data
- [ ] PR job to run compiler and post diagnostics

References / inspiration:
- existing runtime route format in infra repo (see GH link above)
- Konveyor policy compiler notes (mental reference)
- internal cost-model spreadsheet: Confluence link in linked_artifacts

Free-form sketch end. This is intentionally rough — primarily a working spec I want to iterate on in small PRs. Keep it lightweight and reviewable.
